content: Approaching such conversational forecasting problems, however, requires overcoming several inherent modeling challenges. First, conversations are dynamic and their outcome might depend on how subsequent comments interact with each other. Consider the example in Figure FIGREF2: while no individual comment is outright offensive, a human reader can sense a tension emerging from their succession (e.g., dismissive answers to repeated questioning). Thus a forecasting model needs to capture not only the content of each individual comment, but also the relations between comments. Previous work has largely relied on hand-crafted features to capture such relations—e.g., similarity between comments BIBREF16, BIBREF12 or conversation structure BIBREF17, BIBREF18—, though neural attention architectures have also recently shown promise BIBREF19.
